mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport office or notary public of the applicant's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Samoa is not a Contracting State to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; chain: notary public -> Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the originating state -> consular section of the nearest Samoan High Commission or Embassy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or corporate register extract of any corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registered agent of the corporate UBO's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (or Apostille where the third-party state is a Hague Convention party, followed by counter-legalization as accepted by the Samoan Registrar of Companies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed commercial bank maintaining the UBO's primary transactional account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or banker's authentication acceptable to the Samoan licensed registered agent under AML/CFT Act 2019 s 21

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate of the UBO from the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or criminal records authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-onboarding and continuous screening of all directors, shareholders and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Sanctions List, and Samoa's domestic sanctions register administered by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit within the Central Bank of Samoa; domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) attract enhanced due diligence requiring independent wealth confirmation, documentary source-of-funds proof, and senior management approval pursuant to AML/CFT Act 2019 ss 19-21; screening must be repeated on an event-driven basis and at least annually; negative media and adverse legal database checks are compulsory for the Low_Risk_Standard grocery retail risk tier.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry one-stop online clearance portal administered by the Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, with the International Company name reservation channel accessible via SIFSA-licensed registered agents
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registered corporate names must be rendered in Latin script; English and Samoan words are permissible; a foreign-language trade name, including Chinese, must be submitted with a certified English or Samoan transliteration and may be registered only as an auxiliary business name, while the primary corporate name remains in Latin script; Samoan alphabet characters are confined to a e i o u f g l m n p s t v h k r and no name may create phonetic confusion with an existing entity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Samoa or Samoan where implying state endorsement or official connection
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejection notice will cite the conflicting registry entry or the undesirable or misleading significance of the proposed name; the applicant may, within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, file a written appeal affidavit with the Registrar of International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987, accompanied by the prescribed appeal fee; the Registrar must issue a determination within 21 working days; a single 30-day extension of an approved name reservation may be requested in writing before expiry; failure to incorporate within the reservation window requires re-filing of the name clearance with a fresh fee; judicial review of an adverse administrative determination lies to the Supreme Court of Samoa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered-office-only virtual arrangement is permissible for the corporate seat provided a licensed, SIFSA-approved registered agent maintains physical corporate records in Samoa; nevertheless, the ISIC 4721 retail trading licence, the Ministry of Health food-premises clearance and the MCIL business licence require a real, operational physical store in Samoa; pure shell incorporation without commercial substance is not tolerated for local grocery retail and the Registrar of International Companies may commence strike-off proceedings under the International Companies Act 1987 where the company fails to establish trading substance within 12 months.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-to-High: 55% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months of trading, driven by MCIL business-license compliance, Ministry of Health food-premises sanitation checks, and Samoa FIU AML/CFT examinations of the supervising registered agent; probability rises to 65% where UBO due-diligence files are incomplete or where cash-intensive retail transactions trigger enhanced review.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, Part II (Incorporation), sections 6-10; sections 14-20 (registered office and registered agent); sections 30-40 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Level 3, ACB Building, Fa'atoia Street, Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for registration of an international company together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, resulting in the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement. Shares may be issued at par, at a premium, or as no-par shares; consideration may be fully paid, partly paid, or deferred as determined by the directors in accordance with the company's articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscription of [●] ordinary shares by the subscriber be and is hereby accepted, and such shares be allotted as fully paid and non-assessable as authorized by the International Companies Act 1987. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office located at [●], Apia, Samoa, and the corporate registered agent of the Company be and are hereby approved and adopted. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [●] be appointed as director and [●] as company secretary, with authority to execute corporate instruments. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the directors be authorized to file all applications and licenses necessary to commence grocery retail operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Companies Registry Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the chosen name with the mandatory corporate suffix, together with an alternative name, via SIFA's online filing portal or in person at the Registry. The name 'ASIAN SUPERMARKET GROCERY HUB' must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, and must not imply government patronage. A name holding is granted for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Name clearance request form
Statement of business purpose (ISIC 4721 grocery retail and import activity)
Passport copy of the intended subscriber/shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusing similarity, the subscriber may immediately file a new name request or submit a written justification and any consent letter from the conflicting company; a formal refusal may be reviewed by the Registrar on application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarized Execution of the Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa licensed Registered Agent and a Samoa Notary Public / Commissioner for Oaths
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association. The subscriber executes them before a notary public or commissioner for oaths; the registered agent countersigns to evidence acceptance. Where no-par shares are authorized, the articles may omit nominal share capital values. The company's authorized share structure is fixed at one or more classes of ordinary shares.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber's certified passport and proof of residential address
Consent of proposed first director and company secretary
Letter of engagement from the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the executing officer notes an irregular notarization or inconsistent share clause, the document is re-executed within five business days; a rectification deed is used when the defect is clerical only.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application with Government Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files the application for incorporation using the SIFA prescribed form, together with the executed Memorandum and Articles and the registered office/registered agent consents. The filing fee of USD 500 is remitted by bank transfer or card at the SIFA cashier; the fee receipt is attached to the application. The Registrar will issue a defective-notice if the package is incomplete, or proceed to clear the application.
required_dossiers: SIFA incorporation application form
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent's written consent
Registered office address consent (Samoa physical address)
Government filing-fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a defective-notice or information request, the registered agent has 14 days to respond with corrected documents. If the Registrar refuses incorporation, the subscriber may petition SIFA for administrative reconsideration, and thereafter pursue judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Registered Office Endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA; the appointed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once approved, the Registrar enters the international company in the International Companies Register and issues a Certificate of Incorporation with a company number. The registered office and registered agent are recorded as the service address in Samoa. Certified copies of the certificate and register extract are prepared for bank account opening, lease execution and licensing applications.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
International Companies Register extract
Registered office lease or physical location consent
Registered agent's appointment certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a spelling or date error, the registered agent files a request for administrative rectification with SIFA, and the corrected certificate is issued within three business days. If the registered agent ceases to hold a license, a substitute agent must be appointed within seven days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Opening of Statutory Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial director(s) hold the inaugural board meeting, which may be by written resolution. The pro-forma first board resolution is passed to: accept the share subscription, adopt the registered office/registered agent, appoint the initial director(s) and company secretary, and authorize the opening of bank accounts. The company secretary then opens the register of members, register of directors, register of charges, and minutes book at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma board resolution (as set out above)
Share subscription and allotment schedule
Consent to act from each director and secretary
Register of members and directors
Corporate records location statement signed by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a director or officer is disqualified or unavailable, a subsequent board resolution is passed to remove and replace the appointee; any inconsistent registry record is corrected by filing a notice of change with SIFA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Business Licensing Division; Samoa Bureau of Standards (SBS) for imported grocery compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Retail Business Licence under the Business Licences Act 2003 authorizing operation of a physical supermarket/grocery store at the fixed premises in Apia, together with a Food Business Registration Certificate under the Food Act from the Ministry of Health.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Environmental Assessment and Planning Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Permitted Activity Environmental Registration (no full EIA Report required for a small-format grocery store under 500 m2 with no industrial processes); development consent also required from the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with Samoa Water Authority trade-waste sewer standards; cooling/refrigeration systems must use non-ozone-depleting refrigerants and be subject to annual leak checks; vegetable and food waste must be segregated and collected by an approved waste carrier; no untreated wastewater or organic waste may be discharged to coastal waters.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) covering fire escapes, extinguishers and evacuation plan; structural inspection/completion clearance from the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); and an Occupational Safety and Health compliance certificate in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2011, including worker first-aid training and public-liability insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Revenue, Government of Samoa; official e-services portal: Samoa Ministry of Revenue E-Filing system at https://www.samoatax.gov.ws / https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity obtains a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) by filing the prescribed TIN Application Form with the Ministry of Revenue, accompanied by a certificate of incorporation, international company status evidence, memorandum and articles of association, beneficial-owner identification, and registered address. For an International Company conducting only offshore business, no Samoa TIN is mandated solely for income tax, but VAGST registration is required before making taxable supplies in Samoa or importing taxable goods, and the same TIN is then used for VAGST, excise, and customs purposes. Non-resident applicants must appoint a Samoa-based tax agent or local contact person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide the U.S. check-the-box or similar hybrid-mismatch election. An International Company may elect to convert to a Samoa domestic company by special resolution under the International Companies Act 1987 and notification to the Registrar of International Companies, thereby relinquishing its offshore tax-exempt status and becoming subject to ordinary Samoa income tax and VAGST rules. No further deemed classification election is available; anti-avoidance provisions apply to artificial hybrid arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST, also referred to locally as VAT/GST) levied under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 2007 as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 2,000,000 (Samoa tala) annual taxable turnover; compulsory registration also applies to any business importing taxable goods into Samoa for commercial purposes, regardless of turnover, and to non-resident suppliers mandated to collect VAGST on prescribed digital and local supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa currently does not impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, digital stamping, or government-API invoice validation. Registered suppliers must issue a valid VAGST tax invoice showing supplier name, TIN/VAGST number, invoice serial number, date, description of goods/services, taxable amount exclusive of VAGST, the VAGST amount and the total. VAGST returns are filed electronically or manually with the Ministry of Revenue and remittance is due within the statutory return period. The Ministry is gradually implementing integrated e-tools, but no API-based clearance is yet legally mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to the supply of goods that are exported by the registered person from Samoa to a destination outside Samoa within the statutory export time frame, to goods supplied under duty-free/excise-approved arrangements, and to services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa if the services are wholly received and enjoyed outside Samoa. The exporter must maintain evidence that the goods left Samoa and the supply was made in the course of a taxable business; otherwise the standard 15% VAGST rate applies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Samoan Customs Service approved clearance)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from Samoa
Commercial invoice and supplier's VAGST tax invoice
Sales contract or purchase order by overseas buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer evidence from overseas counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to post-clearance documentary audit by the Ministry of Revenue and Samoa Customs. If the exporter cannot substantiate physical export, approved foreign-receipt status, or the absence of on-island consumption, the VAGST is clawed back at the standard 15% rate, plus late payment interest, late filing penalties, and a civil penalty typically not exceeding 200% of the evaded tax. Wilful fraudulent export zero-rating or false inward remittance documentation may lead to criminal prosecution, fines, directors' personal liability, and deregistration from the VAGST register.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) – the unified monetary authority and exchange control administrator under the Exchange Control Act 1987 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is convertible for current account transactions (trade payments, services, dividends, interest) subject to standard documentary verification and tax clearance. Capital account transactions, including direct investment capital injections, portfolio investments, and offshore loans, require prior approval by the Central Bank of Samoa unless conducted by a licensed International Company with a specific exemption. Profit remittance (dividends) is facilitated via authorized dealer banks upon submission of audited financial statements, BOARD resolution, and tax clearance certificates; there are no withholding tax hurdles for International Companies, but foreign remittance fees and CBS transaction reporting apply. The practical convertibility risk is low for retail volumes, but the market is thin, and large one-off transfers may be settled on a T+2 basis.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa’s Exchange Control Act requires all export proceeds to be received through an authorized dealer in Samoa within 30 days from the date of shipment and to be surrendered or credited to a Samoan bank account in WST unless an exemption or retention of foreign currency account is approved by the Central Bank of Samoa. For an International Company engaged in re-export or wholesale of imported goods, conversion of export receipts into WST is mandatory for the fulcrum of the sale, with the standard ratio being 100% conversion within the statutory timeline; however, CBS may permit offshore-retained export earnings if the company demonstrates operational necessity and prior written consent is obtained.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (WST and USD) and Trade Finance Line
Operational Account (WST) and Merchant Acquiring Account for POS/Credit Card settlement
Capital Escrow Account for foreign investment certifiable under the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour
Operational Account (WST) with limited cross-border remittance capability

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low – Offshore digital EMI/FINTECH service providers are not licensed or recognized by the Central Bank of Samoa for local merchant settlement or treasury operations. The Central Bank does not currently maintain a sandbox for inbound cross-border EMI acceptance; any non-bank payment service provider must obtain a Payment Services Provider license under the Financial Institutions Act 2011. No regulated offshore EMI connectivity (Wise, Payoneer, Revolut) can provide Samoan WST clearing or direct local POS/Interac gateway access. Such services may be used only for ancillary remote supplier payments, subject to individual bank approval and not as a primary treasury rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Samoan licensed banks generally require at least one director or an authorized signatory to attend a physical onboarding interview in Samoa for a locally operating retail entity. Remote onboarding is permitted only for an International Company with no domestic commercial substance, where all directors are foreign and the entity is exclusively offshore – then banks may accept certified copies, notarized corporate documents, and a video-conference KYC interview, subject to a bank-level risk committee approval. For a physical grocery ABC hub (ISIC 4721) operating inside Samoa, at least one natural person director (or a appointed resident agent) must be present in Samoa to complete KYC, sign account mandates, and verify the storefront and stock inventory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anonymous or pre-clear 'International Company' ownership structure with low-tier jurisdiction perception
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a statutory declaration from the Samoa International Companies Registrar, a full register of directors and ultimate beneficial owners, a certified copy of the International Company Certificate, and an organizational chart showing the ultimate human beneficiary with a valid passport and passport photograph.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of trade-related inbound funds (concentrated large inbound wire flows without a physical trade trail)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the signed supplier purchase orders, ocean/airway bills, customs entry declarations, cargo import permit, and a projected cash-flow model explaining the timing of inbound equity and the corresponding inventory purchases.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cash-intensive retail activity through POS/credit card rails that could trigger cash smuggling or fraud indicators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Implement and document point-of-sale reconciliation policies, monthly cash deposit receipts, retained transaction logs, and a low-risk retail category justification under the AML/CFT Risk Assessment Framework.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions routed through multiple intermediated corridors to offset domestic WST balances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a currency conversion calendar, copies of all FIU-mandated transaction reports, and a written treasury policy affirming WST settlement for all local retail and trade payables.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the Samoa International Company may be injected via authorized dealer banks using SWIFT MT103 with payment purpose code 'EC' (Equity Capital) or 'DE' (Direct Investment Loan). The routing protocol is: (i) the company's non-resident parent/beneficial owner initiates a wire from a regulated financial institution (e.g., Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia) to the Samoa operational account at ANZ or BSP in WST or USD; (ii) the recipient bank will require a Foreign Investment Certificate (FIC) from the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, a certified board resolution authorizing the capital injection, and a worksheet evidencing the source of funds; (iii) if the transfer exceeds WST 50,000 equivalent, CBS prior approval is required unless the company holds a blanket exemption from the exchange control regulations; (iv) an 'A2' remittance form or electronic declaration must be completed, and the bank will issue a credit advice with the unique FX identification number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for imported Asian condiments and vegetables must be executed exclusively through authorized dealer banks using the SWIFT MT103 (direct credit transfer) or MT202 (for interbank cover). For large, recurring supplier transactions exceeding USD 250,000 per month, a commercial letter of credit (SWIFT MT700) with deferred payment terms is the indemnified clearing rail. All outward remittances must be supported by the supplier proforma invoice, customs import permits, and an exchange control form TR1. The clearing timeline is typically T+1 for WST/USD conversions via Samoa's Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) domestic leg, with an international next-day processing window.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright forward foreign exchange contract with a maturity not exceeding 12 months, approved on a case-by-case basis by the Central Bank of Samoa and executed with a licensed commercial bank (ANZ, BSP, SCB) on a non-speculative, underlying-transaction basis.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered offshore by major global banks referencing WST, but subject to domestic disallowance – formal CBS approval is required before the Samoan entity may enter, and the instrument must be settled only in USD via a wholly offshore corridor with no domestic WST conversion.

Cross-currency swap (WST/USD or WST/AUD) with a licensed bank, provided the swap is fully covered by a defined trade receivable or payable stream, approved by CBS, and documented under ISDA 2002 with the Samoan entity as a rated or collateral-backed counterparty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation statement (annual return) and renewal government fee for an International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based rule: renewal is due on or before each anniversary of incorporation; annual confirmation is filed within 30 days after the anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and late payment penalties apply under the International Companies Act 1987; continued default after formal notice may lead to administrative strike-off from the Samoa International Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit for a standard tax-exempt International Company; audit is required only if the company operates under a separate regulated financial-services license or if shareholders elect an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies are not required to file financial statements; any voluntarily prepared accounts are normally maintained under IFRS or an acceptable private GAAP framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Beneficial Ownership Register must be kept at the registered office and updated within 21 days of any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership. The annual confirmation statement delivered to SIFA confirms current shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners as of the anniversary date; share transfer updates must also be notified promptly to the licensed registered agent.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 – USD 950 per annum for standard licensed registered agent and registered office services in Samoa
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by statute; voluntary certified audit typically USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 for a small grocery-holding structure

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies (tax-exempt regime); 27% standard corporate main tax rate for resident non-international companies
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and dividend withholding tax under the Samoa International Companies Act; no recurrent tax filings or assessment beyond annual registry compliance

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Return Form under the Samoa International Companies Act; filed by the licensed registered agent through the Samoa International Companies Registry electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact name shown on the Certificate of Incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the full official English name as registered; no translation may be substituted except as pre-approved in the certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique registration number issued by the Samoa International Companies Registry
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Copy verbatim from the certificate; this identifier is non-editable and all correspondence must reference it

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Registered Agent and Registered Office
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address in Samoa and the licensed registered agent maintaining the entity's register
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Panama/Samoa licensed agent's street address, not a P.O. Box; the IC cannot act as its own agent

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the company has not derived income from ordinary commercial operations inside Samoa
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: International Companies must confirm no domestic source transactions, no local employees, and no Samoan-resident shareholders

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a daily default penalty of up to WST 100 per day under the International Companies Act; continuing default causes administrative striking-off, loss of legal existence, and reinstatement fees payable to the Registrar.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to non-residents; for non-exempt Samoan resident companies, the Income Tax Act 2012 applies a 15% withholding tax, reducible to 5% to 15% under an applicable DTA depending on shareholding
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate from its home tax authority, submit it to the Samoan paying company and the Samoa Revenue Department (Administered by the Ministry of Revenue), and complete the annual withholding tax exemption declaration before the dividend distribution date; unused treaty positions must be refreshed each year as treaty benefits expire
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Samoan WHT on gross interest and royalties paid by a resident company is 15%; under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand DTAs the rate is generally capped at 10% for both interest and royalties; international companies making such payments are outside the ordinary tax net and suffer no Samoan WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No mandatory Local File/Master File is triggered for a tax-exempt International Company; where an IC nevertheless engages in related-party cross-border trade, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation should be retained once annual related-party transaction value equals or exceeds WST 1,000,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa has adopted Economic Substance Regulations applicable to international companies and offshore companies carrying on geographically mobile activities (banking, insurance, shipping, pure holding, IP, and headquarter services). Physical grocery retail distribution operating in Samoa is a local substantive activity and is not classified as a pure foreign-sourced IP business; nevertheless, all ICs must file an annual economic substance declaration with the Registrar where any deemed activity occurs, demonstrating real management, physical premises, local staff, and operating expenditure in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally misrepresenting import income from Asian grocery sales as non-Samoan foreign source income, or maintaining dual sets of invoices and inventory ledgers to conceal revenue from sales to Samoan residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 200% of tax evaded, a fine not exceeding WST 500,000, and imprisonment up to 7 years under the Income Tax Administration Act 2012
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shadow directors are jointly and severally liable for undeclared tax and penalties; travel bans and asset freezing orders may be imposed pending assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no registered agent, no physical office, no records, and no genuine economic activity in Samoa while routing food import payments and royalties for the purpose of tax avoidance in another jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Registrar cancellation and striking off of the IC, daily penalty of WST 200 until removal, and restoration fee of WST 5,000 plus all arrears
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Continued trading after striking off renders directors personally liable for corporate debts; directors may be subject to a 5-year disqualification from managing any Samoan company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the grocery retail hub as an unlicensed money remittance agent for thousands of Asian expatriate transfers, processing cash deposits without a financial service licence, or failing to submit suspicion reports on bulk cash purchases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Samoan AML/CFT Act 2007, penalties may reach WST 1,000,000 plus civil forfeiture of proceeds; unauthorised financial business may also trigger liquidation proceedings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil is pierced where the company is found to be a mere cloak for individual wrongdoing; responsible directors personally face fines, restitution orders, travel restrictions, and imprisonment up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming tax-exempt international company status while simultaneously operating a local supermarket, engaging Samoan staff, and importing shelf goods within Samoa without disclosing the actual substantive activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty of up to WST 50,000 per year per infraction under Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations, plus reassessment of income tax at the full 27% rate and applicable late payment surcharge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the additional tax if they signed erroneous substance declarations or directed concealment; a history of repeated violations exposes directors to disqualification and removal from the Samoan directors register.
